liu-kun.s: Liu Kun was a Western Jin general, poet and governor of Bingzhou in northern China who held out against the Xiongnu state of Han Zhao after the collapse of Jin authority in the north. He relied on alliances with the Tuoba chief Tuoba Yilu, whom Jin made Duke and then Prince of…

liu-yongfu.s: Liu Yongfu was a Chinese soldier and leader of the Black Flag Army, which fought the French in northern Vietnam in the 1870s and 1880s. In 1895, when the Qing ceded Taiwan to Japan, he joined the short-lived Republic of Formosa and became its leader after President Tang…

ljudevit-posavski.s: Ljudevit Posavski was duke of Lower Pannonia, the Slavic duchy between the Drava and Sava centred on Sisak, under Frankish overlordship. In 819 he rebelled against the harsh rule of the Frankish margrave of Friuli, drawing in neighbouring Slavs and fighting the Duchy of Croatia.

llanbadarn-fawr.s: Llanbadarn Fawr is a village near Aberystwyth in Ceredigion, Wales, the site of an early medieval monastery associated with St Padarn. It was one of the leading church centres of Wales and the seat of a bishop in the early Middle Ages, and a centre of learning in the 11th…

lluis-companys.s: Lluís Companys was a Catalan lawyer and leader of the Republican Left of Catalonia who became president of the Generalitat of Catalonia in 1934 after Francesc Macià. In October 1934 he proclaimed a Catalan State within a federal Spanish republic and was imprisoned.

llywelyn-ap-gruffudd.s: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, known as Llywelyn the Last, was prince of Gwynedd and the only native ruler formally recognised by England as Prince of Wales, by Henry III in the Treaty of Montgomery in 1267. Conflict with Edward I led to English invasions in 1277 and 1282.

llywelyn-the-great.s: Llywelyn the Great, Llywelyn ap Iorwerth, was prince of Gwynedd who made himself the dominant ruler of Wales. He married Joan, daughter of King John of England, and at Aberdyfi in 1216 the other Welsh rulers accepted his overlordship.

loango-bay.s: Loango Bay is a bay on the Atlantic coast of the present-day Republic of the Congo, north of Pointe-Noire. It was the main harbour of the Kingdom of Loango, whose capital Mbanza Loango (Buali) lay nearby.

long-bien.s: Long Biên was an ancient city in the Red River delta near present-day Hanoi, the administrative seat of Chinese-ruled Jiaozhi under the Han and later dynasties. During the revolt of Lý Bí, who proclaimed himself Lý Nam Đế in 544, it served as his base, and he built the Khai…

long-bien-bridge.s: The Long Biên Bridge is a cantilever railway and road bridge across the Red River in Hanoi, built by the French between 1899 and 1902 and originally named after Governor-General Paul Doumer. Part of the railway linking Hanoi with Haiphong and later Yunnan, it was the longest…

long-yunus.s: Long Yunus was a Malay ruler of Pattani descent who unified Kelantan on the east coast of the Malay Peninsula around 1762 and ruled it until his death in 1795. He founded the dynasty that still reigns in Kelantan, whose rulers took the title of sultan in the early 19th century.

lop-nur.s: Lop Nur is a former salt lake, now largely dry, in the eastern Tarim Basin in Xinjiang, China. The ancient oasis kingdom of Kroraina, called Loulan in Chinese, lay on its north-western shore, on the Silk Road between China and the western oases.

lord-chak.s: Lord Chak, recorded as Chan Chak K'ak'nal Ajaw, was a ruler of the Maya city of Uxmal in the Puuc hills of Yucatán around 900. Inscriptions associate him with major building works, and he is thought to have commissioned the Governor's Palace and other monumental structures…

lord-charles-somerset.s: Lord Charles Somerset was a British soldier and politician who governed the Cape Colony from 1814 to 1826. He ruled in an autocratic manner, made English the official language of government and encouraged the settlement of the 1820 Settlers in the Eastern Cape.

lord-meng-of-huang.s: Lord Meng of Huang was a ruler of the small Zhou-era state of Huang in southern Henan in the 7th century BCE. His tomb and that of his wife were excavated at Guangshan in 1983 and yielded fine bronze vessels, jades and lacquerware, which show an aristocratic culture close to…

lord-of-sipan.s: The Lord of Sipán is the name given to a Moche ruler whose undisturbed tomb was discovered in 1987 at Huaca Rajada near Sipán on the north coast of Peru by the archaeologist Walter Alva. Buried around 250 CE with gold, silver and copper regalia and sacrificed attendants, he is…

lordship-of-argos-and-nauplia.s: The Lordship of Argos and Nauplia was a Frankish fief in the Argolid created after the Principality of Achaea captured the strongholds of Leo Sgouros in 1212. Held by the de la Roche family as part of the Duchy of Athens and later by the house of Enghien, it passed in 1388 to…

lothar-franz-von-schonborn.s: Lothar Franz von Schönborn was prince-bishop of Bamberg from 1693 and archbishop-elector of Mainz from 1695 until his death. A great patron of Baroque architecture, he built the New Residence in Bamberg and the palaces of Weissenstein at Pommersfelden and Gaibach.

lough-corrib.s: Lough Corrib is the largest lake in the Republic of Ireland, lying north of Galway city in Connacht. It divided the lowlands of east Galway from Connemara to the west.

louis-fadrique.s: Louis Fadrique was count of Salona in central Greece and a member of the Fadrique family, a branch of the royal house of Sicily. He served as vicar-general of the Catalan duchies of Athens and Neopatras from 1375 to 1381.

louis-faidherbe.s: Louis Faidherbe was a French general and colonial governor of Senegal from 1854 to 1861 and 1863 to 1865. He pushed French rule inland along the Senegal River, fought the Toucouleur Empire of El Hadj Umar Tall and the Wolof kingdoms such as Cayor, and founded the port of Dakar…

louis-ii-of-poitiers.s: Louis II of Poitiers was the last count of Valentinois and Diois in the Rhône valley, of the Poitiers family that had ruled there since the 12th century. Childless and in long conflict with the bishops of Valence and the house of Savoy, he bequeathed his counties to the…

louis-i-duke-of-orleans.s: Louis I, Duke of Orléans, was the younger brother of King Charles VI of France. During the king's bouts of madness he struggled for control of the government with the dukes of Burgundy.

louis-the-blind.s: Louis the Blind, son of Boso, was king of Provence, or Lower Burgundy, from 887 and king of Italy from 900. He was crowned emperor in Rome in 901 as Louis III.

louis-the-child.s: Louis the Child was king of East Francia from 900 to 911, the son of Emperor Arnulf of Carinthia and the last of the East Frankish Carolingians. Crowned at the age of six, he reigned under the guidance of bishops while Magyar raids devastated the kingdom and regional dukes…

louis-viii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis VIII, known as Louis the Hunchback, was duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt and the son of Louis VII the Bearded. He took the side of his father's enemies, and in 1443 he captured his own father and handed him over to the duke of Bavaria-Landshut.

louis-vii-duke-of-bavaria.s: Louis VII the Bearded was duke of Bavaria-Ingolstadt from 1413. Brother of Queen Isabeau of France, he spent years at the French court and returned with great wealth, building the New Castle and the Church of Our Lady in Ingolstadt.

louis-the-stammerer.s: Louis the Stammerer was the son of Charles the Bald, who made him king of Aquitaine in 867. He succeeded his father as king of West Francia in 877 but reigned only until his death in 879.

louis-viii-of-france.s: Louis VIII, called the Lion, was king of France from 1223 to 1226 and son of Philip II Augustus. As prince he invaded England in 1216 at the invitation of rebel barons but was defeated at Lincoln in 1217.

louis-william-margrave-of-baden-baden.s: Louis William, Margrave of Baden-Baden from 1677, was an imperial field marshal known as the Turkish Louis for his victories over the Ottomans, above all at Slankamen in 1691. He later commanded imperial armies on the Rhine in the wars against Louis XIV.

louis-xviii.s: Louis XVIII, brother of Louis XVI, was king of France from 1814 to 1824, apart from the Hundred Days of 1815. Restored by the allies after Napoleon's abdication, he granted the Charter of 1814, which kept a constitutional monarchy with a parliament and preserved many…

louise-michel.s: Louise Michel was a French schoolteacher and anarchist who fought for the Paris Commune of 1871, serving in its National Guard and as an ambulance worker. After its suppression she was deported to New Caledonia, where she taught Kanak people and sympathised with their revolt…

louis-joseph-papineau.s: Louis-Joseph Papineau was a lawyer and leader of the Parti canadien, later the Parti patriote, in Lower Canada, and speaker of its assembly for most of 1815 to 1837. He demanded control of revenues and an elected legislative council, set out in the Ninety-Two Resolutions of 1834.

lower-lusatia.s: Lower Lusatia is a historical region in eastern Germany and western Poland, around Cottbus and the Spree Forest, home to the Lower Sorbian Slavic minority. Ruled as a margraviate under Wettin, Brandenburg and Bohemian lords, it passed with the Bohemian crown and then to Saxony…

lower-styria.s: Lower Styria is the southern, Slovene-speaking part of the historical Duchy of Styria, around Maribor, Celje and Ptuj, now in north-eastern Slovenia. Part of the Habsburg lands for centuries, it was exposed to Ottoman raids in the 15th and 16th centuries.

lu-bu.s: Lü Bu was a Chinese warlord of the late Eastern Han dynasty, famed for his martial skill and notorious for betraying his patrons. He killed Ding Yuan and then the tyrant Dong Zhuo in 192, later seized Xu Province and fought both Yuan Shu, who had proclaimed his own dynasty,…

lu-long.s: Lü Long was the last ruler of Later Liang, the Sixteen Kingdoms state at Guzang in the Hexi Corridor founded by his uncle Lü Guang. He seized the throne in 401 amid succession struggles.

lucas-watzenrode.s: Lucas Watzenrode was prince-bishop of Warmia from 1489 until his death, a powerful figure in Royal Prussia who defended his see's autonomy against both the Teutonic Order and the Polish crown. He was the uncle and patron of Nicolaus Copernicus, whom he brought into the…

lucien-murat.s: Lucien Murat was the second son of Joachim Murat, King of Naples, and Caroline Bonaparte, Napoleon's sister. In 1812 Napoleon granted him the principality of Pontecorvo after Bernadotte gave it up, but he lost it at the Congress of Vienna in 1815.

lucius-aemilius-paullus-macedonicus.s: Lucius Aemilius Paullus Macedonicus was a Roman general who defeated King Perseus of Macedon at Pydna in 168 BCE, ending the Third Macedonian War and the Antigonid monarchy. Rome then divided Macedon into four republics.

lucius-mummius-achaicus.s: Lucius Mummius Achaicus was a Roman consul and general who defeated the Achaean League in 146 BCE. After his victory he destroyed Corinth, killing many of its men, enslaving women and children and shipping its art treasures to Rome.

lucjan-zeligowski.s: Lucjan Żeligowski was a Polish general who in October 1920, in a staged mutiny secretly approved by Józef Piłsudski, seized Vilnius from Lithuania. He proclaimed the Republic of Central Lithuania, nominally for the local Polish-speaking population, which was annexed by Poland…

lucrezia-borgia.s: Lucrezia Borgia was the daughter of Pope Alexander VI and sister of Cesare Borgia. Her first marriage, to Giovanni Sforza, lord of Pesaro, was annulled in 1497, and her second husband, Alfonso of Aragon, was murdered in 1500.

lucus-augusti.s: Lucus Augusti, modern Lugo in Galicia, north-western Spain, was a Roman town founded around 25 BCE. It became a leading centre of Roman Gallaecia and later its provincial capital.

luc-en-diois.s: Luc-en-Diois is a village in the Drôme valley in south-eastern France, the site of Lucus Augusti, one of the two chief towns of the Celtic Vocontii under Roman rule, alongside Vasio (Vaison-la-Romaine). Its role as a centre was later taken over by nearby Dea Augusta, modern Die.

lugdunum-convenarum.s: Lugdunum Convenarum was the Roman town of the Convenae in the upper Garonne valley of south-western France, traditionally founded by Pompey around 72 BCE. It had a forum, temples, baths and a theatre and became an important town of Roman Aquitania.

ludovico-manin.s: Ludovico Manin was the last doge of the Republic of Venice, elected in 1789. In May 1797, under pressure from Napoleon's army, the Great Council voted to dissolve the republic and Manin abdicated, ending more than a thousand years of independence.

ludovico-sforza.s: Ludovico Sforza, called il Moro, ruled the Duchy of Milan as regent from 1480 and as duke from 1494 to 1499. A great patron of the Renaissance, he employed Leonardo da Vinci, who painted the Last Supper and planned an equestrian monument for him.

louis-i-prince-of-anhalt-kothen.s: Louis I, Prince of Anhalt-Köthen from 1603 until his death, was the first ruler of the separate principality of Anhalt-Köthen. ludwig-i-of-bavaria.s: Ludwig I was king of Bavaria from 1825 to 1848. A patron of art and classical architecture, he rebuilt Munich with buildings such as the Glyptothek and the Ludwigstrasse and moved the university there.

ludwig-ii-of-bavaria.s: Ludwig II was king of Bavaria from 1864 to 1886. He was a patron of Richard Wagner and built the romantic castles of Neuschwanstein, Linderhof and Herrenchiemsee.

luigi-carlo-farini.s: Luigi Carlo Farini was an Italian physician, historian and statesman of the Risorgimento. In 1859 he became dictator of Modena and Parma and united them with Romagna as Emilia, which voted in 1860 to join the Kingdom of Sardinia.

luis-abinader.s: Luis Abinader is a Dominican economist and businessman who leads the Modern Revolutionary Party. He won the presidency of the Dominican Republic in 2020, ending sixteen years of government by the Dominican Liberation Party, and was re-elected in 2024.

luis-galvez-rodriguez-de-arias.s: Luis Gálvez Rodríguez de Arias was a Spanish journalist and adventurer in the Amazon. On 14 July 1899, backed by Brazilian rubber interests in Acre, then Bolivian territory, he proclaimed the Independent State of Acre at Puerto Alonso and made himself president.

luis-munoz-marin.s: Luis Muñoz Marín was a Puerto Rican poet, journalist and politician who founded the Popular Democratic Party and became the island's first elected governor in 1948, serving until 1965. He led the creation of the Commonwealth, or Estado Libre Asociado, with its own constitution…

luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva.s: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is a Brazilian trade unionist and founder of the Workers' Party who served as president of Brazil from 2003 to 2010 and again from 2023. luka-bych.s: Luka Bych was a Kuban Cossack politician who led the government of the Kuban People's Republic in 1918–1919. He belonged to the Ukrainian-minded faction of the Kuban Rada that favoured federation with Ukraine and resisted General Denikin's aim of a united Russia.

lulu-al-kabir.s: Lu'lu' al-Kabir was a slave commander and chamberlain of the Hamdanid emirs of Aleppo who became the real power behind them. In 1004 he deposed the last Hamdanid heirs and ruled Aleppo in his own name, balancing between the Fatimid caliphate and the Byzantine Empire and…

luo-fangbo.s: Luo Fangbo was a Hakka scholar and migrant from Guangdong who organised Chinese gold miners in West Borneo. In 1777 he founded the Lanfang kongsi at Mandor near Pontianak, a self-governing community of miners with elected leaders, sometimes called the first republic in Asia.

ly-chieu-hoang.s: Lý Chiêu Hoàng was the only reigning empress in Vietnamese history and the last ruler of the Lý dynasty, enthroned as a child in 1224. In 1225 the regent Trần Thủ Độ arranged her marriage to his young nephew Trần Cảnh and her abdication in his favour.

ly-thai-to.s: Lý Thái Tổ, born Lý Công Uẩn, was the founder of Vietnam's Lý dynasty. Raised in a Buddhist monastery, he became a palace commander and was chosen as king in 1009 after the death of Lê Long Đĩnh, the last Early Lê ruler.

lycomedes-of-mantinea.s: Lycomedes of Mantinea was the leading statesman of the Arcadian League, formed in 370 BCE after Sparta's defeat at Leuctra. With Theban support he organised the federation and the foundation of its new capital, Megalopolis.

lygdamis-ii.s: Lygdamis II was tyrant of Halicarnassus in Caria in the mid-5th century BCE, a grandson of Artemisia I, ruling under Achaemenid overlordship. The historian Herodotus opposed him and went into exile on Samos.

luis-antonio-de-sousa-botelho-mourao.s: Luís António de Sousa Botelho Mourão, known by his title as the Morgado de Mateus, was a Portuguese nobleman who governed the restored Captaincy of São Paulo from 1765 to 1775. leopold-ii-holy-roman-emperor.s: Leopold II, known in Tuscany as Peter Leopold, was a son of Francis Stephen of Lorraine and Maria Theresa who ruled the Grand Duchy of Tuscany from 1765 to 1790. lazar-of-serbia.s: Lazar Hrebeljanović, known as Prince Lazar, was the most powerful Serbian ruler after the collapse of the Serbian Empire, governing Moravian Serbia from about 1371. Allied with Tvrtko I of Bosnia, he defeated the rival lord Nikola Altomanović in 1373.

leopold-iv-prince-of-lippe.s: Leopold IV was the last reigning prince of Lippe, ruling from 1905 after the long succession dispute over the principality was settled in favour of his Lippe-Biesterfeld line. ludger.s: Ludger was a Frisian missionary educated at Utrecht and York who preached among the Frisians and Saxons under Charlemagne. Around 800 he founded a monastery at Werden on the Ruhr, which became an imperial abbey ruling a small territory for a thousand years.
